contexts.text: Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and let it be distinguishing between the waters and the waters ()... The internal man is called the expanse; the Knowledges which are in the internal man, are called the waters above the expanse; and the scientifics of the external man, are called the waters under the expanse. AC 9340:3.
To expand the earth, and to stretch out the heavens. Illustrated.
Therefore the luminaries are said to have been placed in the expanse of the heavens (), that is, in the internal man...
Under Embroider, see this reference.
The Knowledges of good and truth are described by such things as belong to a ship; namely, by the sails ().
I will spread out my palms to Jehovah () = intercession... To spread out the palms is a matter of gesture or action which corresponds to the supplication of the heart...
Then shall the intelligent shine forth as the brightness of the expanse ().
To expand, and to stretch out = to make or create from Divine power.
To praise in the expanse of strength () = from the good of charity which is from the Lord.
To spread the net over him () = to allure by the delights of earthly loves and by reasonings thence.
The cherubs shall be expanding their wings upwards () = the elevation of the truth of faith... For in the expansion of the wings upwards there is the endeavour to elevate themselves...
(Thus) may be known what is signified by to expand and to stretch out the heavens in the following passages.

To stretch out the heavens, and to expand the earth, here, has a like signification to to stretch out and expand the Habitation by means of the curtains; which is to regenerate man; and thus to create or form a new Intellectual in which there is a new Voluntary... AC 9596:6, Illustrated.

In  is described the regeneration of the man of the Celestial Church; and his new Voluntary and Intellectual are described by the expanse. The waters under the expanse and above the expanse are the truths of the external and of the internal man. AC 10238:3.
The expanse of Heaven, from correspondence, = that Intellectual... which is in the light of Heaven.
Expanding and opening (seeds).

The ancient Heavens constitute higher expanses; but the New Heaven an expanse beneath them; for the Heavens are expanses, one above another. In the highest expanses are those who are called celestial Angels... In the expanses under them are those who are called spiritual Angels...

As these prior things continually decrease in activity and expansion down to ultimates; it follows that when their activity and expansion ceases in ultimates, they become substances and matters such as are in earths.
The heat, light, and atmospheres of the natural world only open seeds, keep their productions in expansion...
The heart and lungs, where there are alternate expansions and compressions...
The expansions and compressions (in the organic forms of the mind)...
The stars which appear in the expanse there... AR 65.

For the Heavens are expanses, one above another; and each expanse is like an earth under the feet of those who are there. The highest expanse is like the top of a mountain; the second expanse is beneath it, but extends itself more widely on the sides round about; and the lowest expanse more widely still... AR 876:2. AE 702:2.
The Heaven of those Angels at first, at a distance, appeared to them like an expanse in the clouds... TCR 740.

One morning I looked up into Heaven, and saw above me expanse over expanse; and I saw that the first expanse opened... then the second... and at last the third; and, from enlightenment, I thence perceived, that upon the first expanse were the Angels who constitute the First Heaven; upon the second expanse were the Angels who constitute the Second Heaven; and upon the third expanse were the Angels who constitute the Third Heaven.
It is a most pleasant expansion of all things of the mind, and thence of all things of the bosom.
It expands the inmost things of the mind, and at the same time the inmost things of the body...

In idleness, the mind... is not expanded... Would not the vital expansion of the face shrivel up 1... What keeps the system of the whole body in expansion and tension but the strain of the animus? TCR 694.
Whether the centre is of the expanse, or the expanse of the centre. Explained. TCR 35.
Concerning the centre and the expanse of nature and of life.

The expanse of the centre of life is called the Spiritual World, which subsists from its own Sun; and the expanse of nature is called the natural world, which subsists from its own sun. As spaces and times cannot be predicated of love and wisdom, but states instead of them, the expanse around the Sun of the angelic Heaven is not an extense, but still it is in the extense of the natural sun; and is with the living subjects there according to the receptions; and the receptions are according to the forms.
Now, as the expanse originates from the centre...
They declared, that this state was a state of the expansion of all things of the life of their body...
The delights of love and the pleasant things of wisdom expand minds, and adapt them to reception; as joys and gladnesses expand faces...
The atmospheric expanse from the sun down to the Earth (is in degrees of both kinds).
They have no other notion of God, than as of the nature of the universe in its primes, thus as of its expanse.
If charity and faith exist only above works, they are in an expanse, or in the mind, like...
High over the mountains were a number of expanses...
Expand. Illustrated. AE 315:17. AE 659:24. AE 721:19. AE 799:5.
They are said to be expanded and extended when truths from good are multiplied. AE 304:48. AE 340:22.
The seed... which spreads itself towards the west, etc. () = Divine truth proceeding from the Lord, and received by those...
They that spread a net () = those who want to procure intelligence by means of Knowledges.
To stretch out the curtains of the habitations () = the increments of the Church as to the truths of doctrine.
The expansion and the sign () = manifestation; for spiritual truths are manifested by means of knowledges; because they appear by them to the sight and to the perception of the natural man.
The covering and the expansion () = the external things of that Church.
To spread out and to found () = to establish.
There are six expanses, (three in the Heavens, and three in the Hells). Coro 16.
Above these there are expanses...
They appear as in an expanse, and the expanse as a cloud.
